payload.label: Read rows as Marketplace shelf items
payload.job: Show rows of one kind (tools, workflows, looks, layouts and more) as the Marketplace shelf shows everything my AI can use: title, what it does, who made it, its price and runs, whether it is mine and published, and whether I can use, publish or withdraw it
payload.description: Give kind (one of the kinds in marketplace-kinds.json: tool, workflow, studied-screen, design-component, look, layout, configuration), rows (the source rows of that kind, as their own owner answers them) and published (the ids of that kind this account has published to the shared shelf). Answers items, one shelf item per row: id, key, kind and its label, icon, title (a row's own title when it reads as words, else the action its id names, with the service), job, made_by in the person's words, price and its key value and unit, runs, mine, published and its badge, facts, picture, preview, a link only when it is a web page, open_target, action_input and can (use, publish or withdraw); plus kind ({ id, one, icon }) and kinds (every kind). Which fields are read and how they read is the kinds file's DATA. It reads, publishes and withdraws nothing: reading each kind's rows from the person's store and the shared shelf, paging and searching across kinds, and publishing or withdrawing are the hosted Marketplace's routes and are not run here.

payload.label: Make Marketplace tiles with their icons (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Make tiles of my Marketplace tools and workflows, each with its own icon drawn, for a page or a film to show
payload.description: Reads the tools and workflows as the shelf's readers answer them (two JSON files of { items: [{ id, kind, title, job, steps?, icon? }] }) and the icons folder of an installed lucide-react, and answers one tile per item: id, kind, title, job (cut to 90 characters), steps, icon and svg, the icon's own shape elements (the item's icon, else its kind's icon from marketplace-kinds.json; an alias icon file is followed). Titles that read as machine names are left out. With --out it writes window.<global>=<tiles>; for a page (global TILES unless --global names another). The icon files are read as data, never run. Last line: {"result": {tiles, counts}} or {"error": ...}.

tools.description: The JSON file of tool items, put where {tools} is in the command.

workflows.description: The JSON file of workflow items, put where {workflows} is in the command.

icons.description: The dist/esm/icons folder of an installed lucide-react, put where {icons} is in the command.

out.description: Optional: the page file to write, after --out.

output_schema.description: {"result": {"tiles": [{id, kind, title, job, steps, icon, svg}], "counts": {items, tools, workflows, own_icons}, "written"?}} or {"error": why} with exit 1.

get_it: npm install lucide-react in any folder (its dist/esm/icons folder is --icons)
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Read the tools and workflows with tool:read-rows-as-marketplace-shelf-items or the shelf's own readers and save each as { items }. Tell the person how many tiles were made and how many have their own icon.

verify.requires: a computer with an installed lucide-react icons folder and the person's tool and workflow items saved as files
